task.title: Preserve inert workflow-phase skill bindings
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/737 by carrying authored skill IDs through workflow topology and durable snapshots without granting execution authority.
acceptance_criteria: Accept legacy version-one definitions unchanged and strict version-two phase bindings.
Reject blank, duplicate, and terminal-phase bindings with typed errors.
Preserve exact authored order through preparation, registration, cursor, start, load, reopen, and listing.
Replay legacy start payloads while emitting the new payload version for new runs.

attempts.summary: Established RED preparation and replay coverage.
attempts.diagnostic: Existing phase topology and durable start payloads had no representation for skill bindings.
attempts.patch: Added version compatibility, invalid-binding, topology-preservation, and durable replay tests.

attempts.diagnostic: A new definition version and backward-compatible start payload kept legacy data readable while preserving new authored metadata exactly.
attempts.patch: Extended prepared and registered phases, cursors, and durable snapshots; documented ADR-0018.

outcome.summary: Workflow phases retain validated skill IDs as inert authored metadata without discovering, selecting, composing, executing, or authorizing skills or tools.

lessons: Authored extension metadata must remain inert until a separate caller-owned resolution boundary exists.
Payload versioning can preserve old snapshots without destructive migration.
Exact authored order is data provenance, not precedence or permission semantics.
